BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 9
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/9
- **Title**: gh-7 Change the app logo to the one in the attachment
- **Author**: ajaxspace

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +169
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T07:31:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T07:32:20Z

## PR Description

Closes #7
### What changed
Replaced the app logo with the ticket-provided artwork (Android robot, supplied as a URL in issue #7): Android `mipmap` launcher set (5 densities), full iOS `AppIcon.appiconset`, and the in-app logo on the login screen via a new `AppLogo` widget.

### Key decisions
- The requester's link points to a 200px thumbnail; Wikimedia only serves fixed sizes for this file, so the **same SVG** was rendered at 960px (largest served size) and committed under `tool/logo_source/` — regeneration is offline-reproducible via `tool/generate_icons.py`.
- Robot centered on an opaque white square badge: iOS requires an opaque square icon and a uniform badge keeps Android/iOS consistent. Robot artwork and colors untouched.
- In-app logo rendered through `AppLogo` (asset path owned by the widget); rounded corners via `ClipRRect` in-app only — launcher icons stay unrounded squares.
- Android robot is reproduced from work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License.

### How to verify
```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze && flutter test
```
Logo renders on `LoginPage` (`login_app_logo` widget test); asset ships in the bundle (`test/app_logo_asset_test.dart`); `flutter build apk --debug` succeeds with the new icons.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SRC[issue #7 artwork URL] --> F[tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png]
  F --> GEN[tool/generate_icons.py]
  GEN --> A[assets/images/app_logo.png]
  GEN --> AND[Android mipmap ic_launcher x5]
  GEN --> IOS[iOS AppIcon x15]
  A --> W[AppLogo widget] --> L[LoginPage]
```
</details>

# gh-2: Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)

## Description

## Task

Create a new **mobile Flutter project** in this repository and implement a simple login page.

## Requirements

- Flutter mobile project (Android + iOS targets), clean default structure
- Login page: email/password fields, sign-in button, basic validation and error states
- **Remember me**: persist the session locally so the user stays signed in across app restarts
- **Google sign-in** integration (credential save / autofill where the platform supports it)
- **Apple sign-in** integration (per Apple guidelines)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` pass
- [ ] `flutter test` passes (at least a widget test for the login page)
- [ ] Login page renders on Android and iOS
- [ ] Google and Apple sign-in wired, with saved credentials / autofill where supported

import struct, os, hashlib

def png_info(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        sig = f.read(8)
        assert sig == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', f"{path}: not a PNG"
        f.read(4)  # length
        assert f.read(4) == b'IHDR'
        w,h = struct.unpack('>II', f.read(8))
        bitd, ctype = struct.unpack('>BB', f.read(2))
        return w,h,bitd,ctype

paths = []
for d,sz in [('mdpi',48),('hdpi',72),('xhdpi',96),('xxhdpi',144),('xxxhdpi',192)]:
    paths.append((f'android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-{d}/ic_launcher.png', sz))
ios = [('Icon-App-20x20@1x',20),('Icon-App-20x20@2x',40),('Icon-App-20x20@3x',60),

       ('Icon-App-76x76@2x',152),('Icon-App-83.5x83.5@2x',167),('Icon-App-1024x1024@1x',1024)]
for n,sz in ios:
    paths.append((f'ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/{n}.png', sz))
paths.append(('assets/images/app_logo.png',1024))
paths.append(('tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png',960))

CT = {0:'gray',2:'RGB',3:'palette',4:'gray+A',6:'RGBA'}
bad = 0
for p,exp in paths:
    w,h,bd,ct = png_info(p)
    ok = (w==exp and h==exp)
    if not ok: bad += 1
    print(f"{'OK ' if ok else 'BAD'} {p}: {w}x{h} depth={bd} type={CT.get(ct,ct)} expected={exp}x{exp} sha1={hashlib.sha1(open(p,'rb').read()).hexdigest()[:8]}")
print('bad =', bad)
EOF"}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 9
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/9
- **Title**: gh-7 Change the app logo to the one in the attachment
- **Author**: ajaxspace

- **State**: open

## PR Description

Closes #7
### What changed
Replaced the app logo with the ticket-provided artwork (Android robot, supplied as a URL in issue #7): Android `mipmap` launcher set (5 densities), full iOS `AppIcon.appiconset`, and the in-app logo on the login screen via a new `AppLogo` widget.

### Key decisions
- The requester's link points to a 200px thumbnail; Wikimedia only serves fixed sizes for this file, so the **same SVG** was rendered at 960px (largest served size) and committed under `tool/logo_source/` — regeneration is offline-reproducible via `tool/generate_icons.py`.
- Robot centered on an opaque white square badge: iOS requires an opaque square icon and a uniform badge keeps Android/iOS consistent. Robot artwork and colors untouched.
- In-app logo rendered through `AppLogo` (asset path owned by the widget); rounded corners via `ClipRRect` in-app only — launcher icons stay unrounded squares.
- Android robot is reproduced from work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License.

### How to verify
```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze && flutter test
```
Logo renders on `LoginPage` (`login_app_logo` widget test); asset ships in the bundle (`test/app_logo_asset_test.dart`); `flutter build apk --debug` succeeds with the new icons.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SRC[issue #7 artwork URL] --> F[tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png]
  F --> GEN[tool/generate_icons.py]
  GEN --> A[assets/images/app_logo.png]
  GEN --> AND[Android mipmap ic_launcher x5]
  GEN --> IOS[iOS AppIcon x15]
  A --> W[AppLogo widget] --> L[LoginPage]
```
</details>

# gh-2: Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)

## Description

## Task

Create a new **mobile Flutter project** in this repository and implement a simple login page.

- Flutter mobile project (Android + iOS targets), clean default structure
- Login page: email/password fields, sign-in button, basic validation and error states
- **Remember me**: persist the session locally so the user stays signed in across app restarts
- **Google sign-in** integration (credential save / autofill where the platform supports it)
- **Apple sign-in** integration (per Apple guidelines)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` pass
- [ ] `flutter test` passes (at least a widget test for the login page)
- [ ] Login page renders on Android and iOS
- [ ] Google and Apple sign-in wired, with saved credentials / autofill where supported

import struct, os, hashlib

def png_info(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        sig = f.read(8)
        assert sig == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', f"{path}: not a PNG"
        f.read(4)  # length
        assert f.read(4) == b'IHDR'
        w,h = struct.unpack('>II', f.read(8))
        bitd, ctype = struct.unpack('>BB', f.read(2))
        return w,h,bitd,ctype

paths = []
for d,sz in [('mdpi',48),('hdpi',72),('xhdpi',96),('xxhdpi',144),('xxxhdpi',192)]:

for n,sz in ios:

paths.append(('assets/images/app_logo.png',1024))
paths.append(('tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png',960))

CT = {0:'gray',2:'RGB',3:'palette',4:'gray+A',6:'RGBA'}
bad = 0
for p,exp in paths:

    ok = (w==exp and h==exp)
    if not ok: bad += 1
    print(f"{'OK ' if ok else 'BAD'} {p}: {w}x{h} depth={bd} type={CT.get(ct,ct)} expected={exp}x{exp} sha1={hashlib.sha1(open(p,'rb').read()).hexdigest()[:8]}")

Local verification matches CI: `flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze` (No issues), `flutter test` (37 passed), exit 0. 

Now let me do the exhaustive re-read pass of the changed files and finalize findings. Let me re-check the remaining items:

1. `tool/generate_icons.py` — full read of working tree version (I saw it in the diff; 78 lines). Details:
  - `from PIL import Image; import os` — import order (stdlib after third-party; PEP8 wants stdlib first) — trivial nit, skip or suggestion? It's a tool script; skip.
  - `Image.LANCZOS` — still valid in Pillow 10+ (alias for Image.Resampling.LANCZOS; the deprecated constants removed in Pillow 10 were `Image.ANTIALIAS`, `Image.LINEAR`, `Image.CUBIC`; LANCZOS remains as documented alias). Actually let me double-check: Pillow 9.1.0 deprecated constants `Image.NONE/ZERO...`? The "Resampling" enum introduced in 9.1; constants like `Image.LANCZOS` were NOT removed in 10.0 — the ones removed were ANTIALIAS, CUBIC, LINEAR only. So `Image.LANCZOS` works fine. Not even a nit worth raising; maybe mention modernizing to `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS` as SUGESTION. It works — keep as part of a suggestion only if room. Probably skip to keep findings meaningful.
  - ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO 0.68 — magic constant documented in comment. Fine.
  - `resample(master, size, path)` uses `master.resize` for each size — LANCZOS downscale from 1024 directly to each target — good quality (single-step).
  - iOS 1024 marketing icon: RGB no alpha — App Store compliant. Good.
  - The script has `print` — fine for a CLI tool.
  - No `if not SOURCE exists` error handling — if source missing, PIL raises FileNotFoundError with a clear message. Fine.
  - Determinism: PIL PNG save is deterministic given same input/PIL version. OK.

2. `AppLogo` widget:
  - `Image.asset` without `semanticLabel` — accessibility: screen reader users get no description of the logo. flutter_lints doesn't enforce, but it's a legit a11y suggestion (Image has `semanticLabel` param, or wrap in Semantics). SUGESTION.
  - Hardcoded `BorderRadius.circular(20)` regardless of `size` — at size 96 radius 20 (~21%) looks consistent, but consumers passing a smaller `size` get proportionally heavier rounding. Derive from size. SUGESTION.
  - No `cacheWidth`: decodes full 1024x1024 (≈4MB decoded) for a 96 logical px widget. `cacheWidth: (size * MediaQuery.devicePixelRatioOf(context)).round()` would cut decode cost. SUGESTION (perf).
  - `fit: BoxFit.cover` — image is square, box is square → no-op but harmless/defensive. Not worth flaging? Could mention in passing within a comment file. Skip.

3. Tests:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the DM Tools app logo + all launcher icon sizes.

Source artwork: the Android robot logo, provided by the ticket requester
(https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Android_robot.svg/200px-Android_robot.svg.png
— same SVG rendered at 960px, the largest Wikimedia-served size; committed at
tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png). The Android robot is reproduced from
work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0
Attribution License.

The robot is centered on an opaque white square badge (platform icon masks
require an opaque square; the badge keeps Android and iOS consistent), and
all sizes are emitted:

  - assets/images/app_logo.png           (1024x1024 master, in-app)
  - android mipmap ic_launcher.png        (48/72/96/144/192)
  - iOS AppIcon.appiconset PNGs           (all sizes in Contents.json)

Deterministic: no randomness, no network (uses the committed source).
"""
from PIL import Image
import os

MASTER = 1024
ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO = 0.68          # robot height as a fraction of the badge
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SOURCE = os.path.join(ROOT, 'tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png')


def build_master():
    robot = Image.open(SOURCE).convert('RGBA')
    h = round(MASTER * ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO)
    w = round(h * robot.width / robot.height)
    robot = robot.resize((w, h), Image.LANCZOS)

    badge = Image.new('RGB', (MASTER, MASTER), (255, 255, 255))
    offset = ((MASTER - w) // 2, (MASTER - h) // 2)
    badge.paste(robot, offset, robot)   # paste with alpha as mask
    return badge


def resample(master, size, path):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    out = master.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS)
    out.save(path, 'PNG')
    print(f'wrote {path} ({size}x{size})')


def main():
    master = build_master()

    resample(master, MASTER, os.path.join(ROOT, 'assets/images/app_logo.png'))

    android = [
        ('mipmap-mdpi', 48), ('mipmap-hdpi', 72), ('mipmap-xhdpi', 96),
        ('mipmap-xxhdpi', 144), ('mipmap-xxxhdpi', 192),
    ]
    for density, size in android:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'android/app/src/main/res/{density}/ic_launcher.png'))

    ios_sizes = [
        ('Icon-App-20x20@1x', 20), ('Icon-App-20x20@2x', 40),
        ('Icon-App-20x20@3x', 60), ('Icon-App-29x29@1x', 29),
        ('Icon-App-29x29@2x', 58), ('Icon-App-29x29@3x', 87),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@1x', 40), ('Icon-App-40x40@2x', 80),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@3x', 120), ('Icon-App-60x60@2x', 120),
        ('Icon-App-60x60@3x', 180), ('Icon-App-76x76@1x', 76),
        ('Icon-App-76x76@2x', 152), ('Icon-App-83.5x83.5@2x', 167),
        ('Icon-App-1024x1024@1x', 1024),
    ]
    for name, size in ios_sizes:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/{name}.png'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# PR CI for the DMTools machine loop.
#
# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml
#       -> workflow_run: workflows: ['CI']       (this file's `name:`)
#   sm-kicker.yml -> ci_workflow: ci.yml          (this file name)
#   machine-sm.yml -> validation-checks: ["test"] (the `test` job id below,
#                                                    the required context)
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)
          PY
=== README ===
# dm_tools_app_example

Flutter mobile app (Android + iOS) with a login page: email/password sign-in,
**Remember me** session persistence, Google sign-in, and Sign in with Apple.

## Run

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter run            # device or emulator with Android/iOS target
flutter test           # unit + widget tests
flutter analyze
```

## Architecture

- `lib/domain/` — `AuthUser`, `AuthException`, credential validation rules
- `lib/services/` — `AuthGateway` (provider operations) → `DefaultAuthService`
  (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`)
- `lib/ui/` — `LoginPage` (form, remember-me, federated buttons), `HomePage`

Sign-in flows delegate to `AuthGateway`; the service persists the session when
**Remember me** is on, and `DmToolsApp` restores it on startup (login page is
skipped when a session exists).

## Provider setup

- **Google** — `google_sign_in` 7.x needs an OAuth client for Android
  (`google-services.json` / SHA-1 in the console) and iOS (URL scheme from the
  client ID). Without it the button compiles but sign-in fails at runtime.
- **Apple** — the `com.apple.developer.applesignin` entitlement is already
  wired into `ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements` and the Xcode project; enable the
  capability for your App ID in the Apple developer portal. The button is
  hidden automatically where Sign in with Apple is unavailable.
- **Email/password** — local stub (no backend); replace the body of
  `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` with a real identity API call.
- Password managers / autofill: the form uses an `AutofillGroup` and finishes
  the autofill context on success, so platforms that support it offer to save
  and later autofill credentials.

Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 9
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/9
- **Title**: gh-7 Change the app logo to the one in the attachment
- **Author**: ajaxspace

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +169
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T07:31:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T07:32:20Z

## PR Description

Closes #7
### What changed
Replaced the app logo with the ticket-provided artwork (Android robot, supplied as a URL in issue #7): Android `mipmap` launcher set (5 densities), full iOS `AppIcon.appiconset`, and the in-app logo on the login screen via a new `AppLogo` widget.

### Key decisions
- The requester's link points to a 200px thumbnail; Wikimedia only serves fixed sizes for this file, so the **same SVG** was rendered at 960px (largest served size) and committed under `tool/logo_source/` — regeneration is offline-reproducible via `tool/generate_icons.py`.
- Robot centered on an opaque white square badge: iOS requires an opaque square icon and a uniform badge keeps Android/iOS consistent. Robot artwork and colors untouched.
- In-app logo rendered through `AppLogo` (asset path owned by the widget); rounded corners via `ClipRRect` in-app only — launcher icons stay unrounded squares.
- Android robot is reproduced from work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License.

### How to verify
```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze && flutter test
```
Logo renders on `LoginPage` (`login_app_logo` widget test); asset ships in the bundle (`test/app_logo_asset_test.dart`); `flutter build apk --debug` succeeds with the new icons.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SRC[issue #7 artwork URL] --> F[tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png]
  F --> GEN[tool/generate_icons.py]
  GEN --> A[assets/images/app_logo.png]
  GEN --> AND[Android mipmap ic_launcher x5]
  GEN --> IOS[iOS AppIcon x15]
  A --> W[AppLogo widget] --> L[LoginPage]
```
</details>

# gh-2: Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)

## Description

## Task

Create a new **mobile Flutter project** in this repository and implement a simple login page.

## Requirements

- Flutter mobile project (Android + iOS targets), clean default structure
- Login page: email/password fields, sign-in button, basic validation and error states
- **Remember me**: persist the session locally so the user stays signed in across app restarts
- **Google sign-in** integration (credential save / autofill where the platform supports it)
- **Apple sign-in** integration (per Apple guidelines)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` pass
- [ ] `flutter test` passes (at least a widget test for the login page)
- [ ] Login page renders on Android and iOS
- [ ] Google and Apple sign-in wired, with saved credentials / autofill where supported

import struct, os, hashlib

def png_info(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        sig = f.read(8)
        assert sig == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', f"{path}: not a PNG"
        f.read(4)  # length
        assert f.read(4) == b'IHDR'
        w,h = struct.unpack('>II', f.read(8))
        bitd, ctype = struct.unpack('>BB', f.read(2))
        return w,h,bitd,ctype

paths = []
for d,sz in [('mdpi',48),('hdpi',72),('xhdpi',96),('xxhdpi',144),('xxxhdpi',192)]:
    paths.append((f'android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-{d}/ic_launcher.png', sz))
ios = [('Icon-App-20x20@1x',20),('Icon-App-20x20@2x',40),('Icon-App-20x20@3x',60),

       ('Icon-App-76x76@2x',152),('Icon-App-83.5x83.5@2x',167),('Icon-App-1024x1024@1x',1024)]
for n,sz in ios:
    paths.append((f'ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/{n}.png', sz))
paths.append(('assets/images/app_logo.png',1024))
paths.append(('tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png',960))

CT = {0:'gray',2:'RGB',3:'palette',4:'gray+A',6:'RGBA'}
bad = 0
for p,exp in paths:
    w,h,bd,ct = png_info(p)
    ok = (w==exp and h==exp)
    if not ok: bad += 1
    print(f"{'OK ' if ok else 'BAD'} {p}: {w}x{h} depth={bd} type={CT.get(ct,ct)} expected={exp}x{exp} sha1={hashlib.sha1(open(p,'rb').read()).hexdigest()[:8]}")
print('bad =', bad)
EOF"}

Local verification matches CI: `flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze` (No issues), `flutter test` (37 passed), exit 0. 

Now let me do the exhaustive re-read pass of the changed files and finalize findings. Let me re-check the remaining items:

1. `tool/generate_icons.py` — full read of working tree version (I saw it in the diff; 78 lines). Details:
  - `from PIL import Image; import os` — import order (stdlib after third-party; PEP8 wants stdlib first) — trivial nit, skip or suggestion? It's a tool script; skip.
  - `Image.LANCZOS` — still valid in Pillow 10+ (alias for Image.Resampling.LANCZOS; the deprecated constants removed in Pillow 10 were `Image.ANTIALIAS`, `Image.LINEAR`, `Image.CUBIC`; LANCZOS remains as documented alias). Actually let me double-check: Pillow 9.1.0 deprecated constants `Image.NONE/ZERO...`? The "Resampling" enum introduced in 9.1; constants like `Image.LANCZOS` were NOT removed in 10.0 — the ones removed were ANTIALIAS, CUBIC, LINEAR only. So `Image.LANCZOS` works fine. Not even a nit worth raising; maybe mention modernizing to `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS` as SUGESTION. It works — keep as part of a suggestion only if room. Probably skip to keep findings meaningful.
  - ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO 0.68 — magic constant documented in comment. Fine.
  - `resample(master, size, path)` uses `master.resize` for each size — LANCZOS downscale from 1024 directly to each target — good quality (single-step).
  - iOS 1024 marketing icon: RGB no alpha — App Store compliant. Good.
  - The script has `print` — fine for a CLI tool.
  - No `if not SOURCE exists` error handling — if source missing, PIL raises FileNotFoundError with a clear message. Fine.
  - Determinism: PIL PNG save is deterministic given same input/PIL version. OK.

2. `AppLogo` widget:
  - `Image.asset` without `semanticLabel` — accessibility: screen reader users get no description of the logo. flutter_lints doesn't enforce, but it's a legit a11y suggestion (Image has `semanticLabel` param, or wrap in Semantics). SUGESTION.
  - Hardcoded `BorderRadius.circular(20)` regardless of `size` — at size 96 radius 20 (~21%) looks consistent, but consumers passing a smaller `size` get proportionally heavier rounding. Derive from size. SUGESTION.
  - No `cacheWidth`: decodes full 1024x1024 (≈4MB decoded) for a 96 logical px widget. `cacheWidth: (size * MediaQuery.devicePixelRatioOf(context)).round()` would cut decode cost. SUGESTION (perf).
  - `fit: BoxFit.cover` — image is square, box is square → no-op but harmless/defensive. Not worth flaging? Could mention in passing within a comment file. Skip.

3. Tests:
  - `app_logo_asset_test.dart` — asserts bundle ships + square + 1024px. Meaningful, not string-only. Good.
  - login_page_test new group — asserts Image present with correct AssetImage and positioned above headline. Good coverage.
  - Duplication: `AppLogo.assetName` used everywhere — good, no duplication.
  - One nit: `await tester.pump()` after pumpWidget in logo test — fine.

4. `pubspec.yaml` — assets section added with comment; fine. The template's commented example below remains — fine (pre-existing).

5. Scope: PR is exactly the ticket scope (logo change), +tests, +generator. No scope creep. Android robot attribution included in PR description AND script docstring — but not in a LICENSE/NOTICE file at repo root. CC-BY 3.0 attribution requirement: attribution should be reasonably visible; for an app, typically in About screen or metadata. Currently only in a dev tool docstring. This is a legitimate ⚠️ IMPORTANT? Hmm. The CC-BY 3.0 license requires attribution "in any reasonable manner" — a docstring in the generator + PR description is arguably reasonable for a code repo, but end-user-facing apps typically need attribution in-app or in the store listing. This is a judgement call; raising it as SUGESTION (add to README or an in-app About/licenses section) seems right — not blocking. Actually let me check README to see if there's a spot. Let me quickly check README and whether Flutter's generated NOTICE handles it (no — it's a PNG asset, not a pub package).

  Actually — I should be careful: is the claim "Android robot is CC-BY 3.0" verifiable? It's commonly known the Android robot is CC-BY 3.0 per Google's brand guidelines (developer.android.com/distribute/marketing-tools/brand-guidelines: "The Android robot is reproduced or modified from work created and shared by Google and used according to terms described in the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License"). That's standard text. Fine — the PR itself includes this attribution text. I'll suggest persisting attribution in README for end-user visibility. SUGESTION.

6. Check README to confirm no attribution section exists. And check android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest roundIcon? Default template has only android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher". Fine.

7. `login_page.dart` — `const Center(child: AppLogo(key: Key('login_app_logo'))` — Key instead of ValueKey: consistent with existing code (all other Keys use `Key(...)`). Consistent. Fine.

8. Missing: `web/` icon? No web target in repo (only android/ios). Fine.

9. The iOS `Contents.json` not regenerated but matches the 15 files — verified above.

10. Old template also had `Icon-App-64x64@1x.png`? No — default Flutter template AppIcon set has exactly the 19 entries/15 unique files above. All replaced. Verified via git diff stat: 15 iOS PNGs changed. Contents.json unchanged and still valid. 

11. Anything about `assets/images/app_logo.png` being 29830 bytes — identical blob to iOS 1024 icon (sha1 2cd51df0 both) — duplication is intended (master re-used), zero extra cost.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the DM Tools app logo + all launcher icon sizes.

Source artwork: the Android robot logo, provided by the ticket requester
(https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Android_robot.svg/200px-Android_robot.svg.png
— same SVG rendered at 960px, the largest Wikimedia-served size; committed at
tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png). The Android robot is reproduced from
work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0
Attribution License.

The robot is centered on an opaque white square badge (platform icon masks
require an opaque square; the badge keeps Android and iOS consistent), and
all sizes are emitted:

  - assets/images/app_logo.png           (1024x1024 master, in-app)
  - android mipmap ic_launcher.png        (48/72/96/144/192)
  - iOS AppIcon.appiconset PNGs           (all sizes in Contents.json)

Deterministic: no randomness, no network (uses the committed source).
"""
from PIL import Image
import os

MASTER = 1024
ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO = 0.68          # robot height as a fraction of the badge
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SOURCE = os.path.join(ROOT, 'tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png')


def build_master():
    robot = Image.open(SOURCE).convert('RGBA')
    h = round(MASTER * ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO)
    w = round(h * robot.width / robot.height)
    robot = robot.resize((w, h), Image.LANCZOS)

    badge = Image.new('RGB', (MASTER, MASTER), (255, 255, 255))
    offset = ((MASTER - w) // 2, (MASTER - h) // 2)
    badge.paste(robot, offset, robot)   # paste with alpha as mask
    return badge


def resample(master, size, path):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    out = master.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS)
    out.save(path, 'PNG')
    print(f'wrote {path} ({size}x{size})')


def main():
    master = build_master()

    resample(master, MASTER, os.path.join(ROOT, 'assets/images/app_logo.png'))

    android = [
        ('mipmap-mdpi', 48), ('mipmap-hdpi', 72), ('mipmap-xhdpi', 96),
        ('mipmap-xxhdpi', 144), ('mipmap-xxxhdpi', 192),
    ]
    for density, size in android:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'android/app/src/main/res/{density}/ic_launcher.png'))

    ios_sizes = [
        ('Icon-App-20x20@1x', 20), ('Icon-App-20x20@2x', 40),
        ('Icon-App-20x20@3x', 60), ('Icon-App-29x29@1x', 29),
        ('Icon-App-29x29@2x', 58), ('Icon-App-29x29@3x', 87),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@1x', 40), ('Icon-App-40x40@2x', 80),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@3x', 120), ('Icon-App-60x60@2x', 120),
        ('Icon-App-60x60@3x', 180), ('Icon-App-76x76@1x', 76),
        ('Icon-App-76x76@2x', 152), ('Icon-App-83.5x83.5@2x', 167),
        ('Icon-App-1024x1024@1x', 1024),
    ]
    for name, size in ios_sizes:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/{name}.png'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

=== README ===
# dm_tools_app_example

Flutter mobile app (Android + iOS) with a login page: email/password sign-in,
**Remember me** session persistence, Google sign-in, and Sign in with Apple.

## Run

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter run            # device or emulator with Android/iOS target
flutter test           # unit + widget tests
flutter analyze
```

## Architecture

- `lib/domain/` — `AuthUser`, `AuthException`, credential validation rules
- `lib/services/` — `AuthGateway` (provider operations) → `DefaultAuthService`
  (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`)
- `lib/ui/` — `LoginPage` (form, remember-me, federated buttons), `HomePage`

Sign-in flows delegate to `AuthGateway`; the service persists the session when
**Remember me** is on, and `DmToolsApp` restores it on startup (login page is
skipped when a session exists).

## Provider setup

- **Google** — `google_sign_in` 7.x needs an OAuth client for Android
  (`google-services.json` / SHA-1 in the console) and iOS (URL scheme from the
  client ID). Without it the button compiles but sign-in fails at runtime.
- **Apple** — the `com.apple.developer.applesignin` entitlement is already
  wired into `ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements` and the Xcode project; enable the
  capability for your App ID in the Apple developer portal. The button is
  hidden automatically where Sign in with Apple is unavailable.
- **Email/password** — local stub (no backend); replace the body of
  `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` with a real identity API call.
- Password managers / autofill: the form uses an `AutofillGroup` and finishes
  the autofill context on success, so platforms that support it offer to save
  and later autofill credentials.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 9
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/9
- **Title**: gh-7 Change the app logo to the one in the attachment
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-7` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 28
- **Additions**: +169
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T07:31:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T07:32:20Z

## PR Description

Closes #7
### What changed
Replaced the app logo with the ticket-provided artwork (Android robot, supplied as a URL in issue #7): Android `mipmap` launcher set (5 densities), full iOS `AppIcon.appiconset`, and the in-app logo on the login screen via a new `AppLogo` widget.

### Key decisions
- The requester's link points to a 200px thumbnail; Wikimedia only serves fixed sizes for this file, so the **same SVG** was rendered at 960px (largest served size) and committed under `tool/logo_source/` — regeneration is offline-reproducible via `tool/generate_icons.py`.
- Robot centered on an opaque white square badge: iOS requires an opaque square icon and a uniform badge keeps Android/iOS consistent. Robot artwork and colors untouched.
- In-app logo rendered through `AppLogo` (asset path owned by the widget); rounded corners via `ClipRRect` in-app only — launcher icons stay unrounded squares.
- Android robot is reproduced from work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License.

### How to verify
```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze && flutter test
```
Logo renders on `LoginPage` (`login_app_logo` widget test); asset ships in the bundle (`test/app_logo_asset_test.dart`); `flutter build apk --debug` succeeds with the new icons.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SRC[issue #7 artwork URL] --> F[tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png]
  F --> GEN[tool/generate_icons.py]
  GEN --> A[assets/images/app_logo.png]
  GEN --> AND[Android mipmap ic_launcher x5]
  GEN --> IOS[iOS AppIcon x15]
  A --> W[AppLogo widget] --> L[LoginPage]
```
</details>

# gh-2: Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)

## Description

## Task

Create a new **mobile Flutter project** in this repository and implement a simple login page.

## Requirements

- Flutter mobile project (Android + iOS targets), clean default structure
- Login page: email/password fields, sign-in button, basic validation and error states
- **Remember me**: persist the session locally so the user stays signed in across app restarts
- **Google sign-in** integration (credential save / autofill where the platform supports it)
- **Apple sign-in** integration (per Apple guidelines)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` pass
- [ ] `flutter test` passes (at least a widget test for the login page)
- [ ] Login page renders on Android and iOS
- [ ] Google and Apple sign-in wired, with saved credentials / autofill where supported

blocks.text:
Local verification matches CI: `flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze` (No issues), `flutter test` (37 passed), exit 0. 

Now let me do the exhaustive re-read pass of the changed files and finalize findings. Let me re-check the remaining items:

1. `tool/generate_icons.py` — full read of working tree version (I saw it in the diff; 78 lines). Details:
  - `from PIL import Image; import os` — import order (stdlib after third-party; PEP8 wants stdlib first) — trivial nit, skip or suggestion? It's a tool script; skip.
  - `Image.LANCZOS` — still valid in Pillow 10+ (alias for Image.Resampling.LANCZOS; the deprecated constants removed in Pillow 10 were `Image.ANTIALIAS`, `Image.LINEAR`, `Image.CUBIC`; LANCZOS remains as documented alias). Actually let me double-check: Pillow 9.1.0 deprecated constants `Image.NONE/ZERO...`? The "Resampling" enum introduced in 9.1; constants like `Image.LANCZOS` were NOT removed in 10.0 — the ones removed were ANTIALIAS, CUBIC, LINEAR only. So `Image.LANCZOS` works fine. Not even a nit worth raising; maybe mention modernizing to `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS` as SUGESTION. It works — keep as part of a suggestion only if room. Probably skip to keep findings meaningful.
  - ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO 0.68 — magic constant documented in comment. Fine.
  - `resample(master, size, path)` uses `master.resize` for each size — LANCZOS downscale from 1024 directly to each target — good quality (single-step).
  - iOS 1024 marketing icon: RGB no alpha — App Store compliant. Good.
  - The script has `print` — fine for a CLI tool.
  - No `if not SOURCE exists` error handling — if source missing, PIL raises FileNotFoundError with a clear message. Fine.
  - Determinism: PIL PNG save is deterministic given same input/PIL version. OK.

2. `AppLogo` widget:
  - `Image.asset` without `semanticLabel` — accessibility: screen reader users get no description of the logo. flutter_lints doesn't enforce, but it's a legit a11y suggestion (Image has `semanticLabel` param, or wrap in Semantics). SUGESTION.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the DM Tools app logo + all launcher icon sizes.

Source artwork: the Android robot logo, provided by the ticket requester
(https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Android_robot.svg/200px-Android_robot.svg.png
— same SVG rendered at 960px, the largest Wikimedia-served size; committed at
tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png). The Android robot is reproduced from
work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0
Attribution License.

The robot is centered on an opaque white square badge (platform icon masks
require an opaque square; the badge keeps Android and iOS consistent), and
all sizes are emitted:

  - assets/images/app_logo.png           (1024x1024 master, in-app)
  - android mipmap ic_launcher.png        (48/72/96/144/192)
  - iOS AppIcon.appiconset PNGs           (all sizes in Contents.json)

Deterministic: no randomness, no network (uses the committed source).
"""
from PIL import Image
import os

MASTER = 1024
ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO = 0.68          # robot height as a fraction of the badge
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SOURCE = os.path.join(ROOT, 'tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png')


def build_master():
    robot = Image.open(SOURCE).convert('RGBA')
    h = round(MASTER * ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO)
    w = round(h * robot.width / robot.height)
    robot = robot.resize((w, h), Image.LANCZOS)

    badge = Image.new('RGB', (MASTER, MASTER), (255, 255, 255))
    offset = ((MASTER - w) // 2, (MASTER - h) // 2)
    badge.paste(robot, offset, robot)   # paste with alpha as mask
    return badge


def resample(master, size, path):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    out = master.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS)
    out.save(path, 'PNG')
    print(f'wrote {path} ({size}x{size})')


def main():
    master = build_master()

    resample(master, MASTER, os.path.join(ROOT, 'assets/images/app_logo.png'))

    android = [
        ('mipmap-mdpi', 48), ('mipmap-hdpi', 72), ('mipmap-xhdpi', 96),
        ('mipmap-xxhdpi', 144), ('mipmap-xxxhdpi', 192),
    ]
    for density, size in android:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'android/app/src/main/res/{density}/ic_launcher.png'))

    ios_sizes = [
        ('Icon-App-20x20@1x', 20), ('Icon-App-20x20@2x', 40),
        ('Icon-App-20x20@3x', 60), ('Icon-App-29x29@1x', 29),
        ('Icon-App-29x29@2x', 58), ('Icon-App-29x29@3x', 87),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@1x', 40), ('Icon-App-40x40@2x', 80),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@3x', 120), ('Icon-App-60x60@2x', 120),
        ('Icon-App-60x60@3x', 180), ('Icon-App-76x76@1x', 76),
        ('Icon-App-76x76@2x', 152), ('Icon-App-83.5x83.5@2x', 167),
        ('Icon-App-1024x1024@1x', 1024),
    ]
    for name, size in ios_sizes:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/{name}.png'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

name: CI

on:

  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        run: |

=== README ===
# dm_tools_app_example

Flutter mobile app (Android + iOS) with a login page: email/password sign-in,
**Remember me** session persistence, Google sign-in, and Sign in with Apple.

## Run

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter run            # device or emulator with Android/iOS target
flutter test           # unit + widget tests
flutter analyze
```

## Architecture

- `lib/domain/` — `AuthUser`, `AuthException`, credential validation rules
- `lib/services/` — `AuthGateway` (provider operations) → `DefaultAuthService`
  (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`)
- `lib/ui/` — `LoginPage` (form, remember-me, federated buttons), `HomePage`

Sign-in flows delegate to `AuthGateway`; the service persists the session when
**Remember me** is on, and `DmToolsApp` restores it on startup (login page is
skipped when a session exists).

## Provider setup

- **Google** — `google_sign_in` 7.x needs an OAuth client for Android
  (`google-services.json` / SHA-1 in the console) and iOS (URL scheme from the
  client ID). Without it the button compiles but sign-in fails at runtime.
- **Apple** — the `com.apple.developer.applesignin` entitlement is already
  wired into `ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements` and the Xcode project; enable the
  capability for your App ID in the Apple developer portal. The button is
  hidden automatically where Sign in with Apple is unavailable.
- **Email/password** — local stub (no backend); replace the body of
  `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` with a real identity API call.
- Password managers / autofill: the form uses an `AutofillGroup` and finishes
  the autofill context on success, so platforms that support it offer to save
  and later autofill credentials.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-7` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +169
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T07:31:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T07:32:20Z

## PR Description

Closes #7
### What changed
Replaced the app logo with the ticket-provided artwork (Android robot, supplied as a URL in issue #7): Android `mipmap` launcher set (5 densities), full iOS `AppIcon.appiconset`, and the in-app logo on the login screen via a new `AppLogo` widget.

### Key decisions
- The requester's link points to a 200px thumbnail; Wikimedia only serves fixed sizes for this file, so the **same SVG** was rendered at 960px (largest served size) and committed under `tool/logo_source/` — regeneration is offline-reproducible via `tool/generate_icons.py`.
- Robot centered on an opaque white square badge: iOS requires an opaque square icon and a uniform badge keeps Android/iOS consistent. Robot artwork and colors untouched.
- In-app logo rendered through `AppLogo` (asset path owned by the widget); rounded corners via `ClipRRect` in-app only — launcher icons stay unrounded squares.
- Android robot is reproduced from work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License.

### How to verify
```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze && flutter test
```
Logo renders on `LoginPage` (`login_app_logo` widget test); asset ships in the bundle (`test/app_logo_asset_test.dart`); `flutter build apk --debug` succeeds with the new icons.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SRC[issue #7 artwork URL] --> F[tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png]
  F --> GEN[tool/generate_icons.py]
  GEN --> A[assets/images/app_logo.png]
  GEN --> AND[Android mipmap ic_launcher x5]
  GEN --> IOS[iOS AppIcon x15]
  A --> W[AppLogo widget] --> L[LoginPage]
```
</details>

## Description

## Task

Create a new **mobile Flutter project** in this repository and implement a simple login page.

- Flutter mobile project (Android + iOS targets), clean default structure
- Login page: email/password fields, sign-in button, basic validation and error states
- **Remember me**: persist the session locally so the user stays signed in across app restarts
- **Google sign-in** integration (credential save / autofill where the platform supports it)
- **Apple sign-in** integration (per Apple guidelines)

- [ ] `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` pass
- [ ] `flutter test` passes (at least a widget test for the login page)
- [ ] Login page renders on Android and iOS
- [ ] Google and Apple sign-in wired, with saved credentials / autofill where supported

Local verification matches CI: `flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze` (No issues), `flutter test` (37 passed), exit 0. 

Now let me do the exhaustive re-read pass of the changed files and finalize findings. Let me re-check the remaining items:

1. `tool/generate_icons.py` — full read of working tree version (I saw it in the diff; 78 lines). Details:
  - `from PIL import Image; import os` — import order (stdlib after third-party; PEP8 wants stdlib first) — trivial nit, skip or suggestion? It's a tool script; skip.
  - `Image.LANCZOS` — still valid in Pillow 10+ (alias for Image.Resampling.LANCZOS; the deprecated constants removed in Pillow 10 were `Image.ANTIALIAS`, `Image.LINEAR`, `Image.CUBIC`; LANCZOS remains as documented alias). Actually let me double-check: Pillow 9.1.0 deprecated constants `Image.NONE/ZERO...`? The "Resampling" enum introduced in 9.1; constants like `Image.LANCZOS` were NOT removed in 10.0 — the ones removed were ANTIALIAS, CUBIC, LINEAR only. So `Image.LANCZOS` works fine. Not even a nit worth raising; maybe mention modernizing to `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS` as SUGESTION. It works — keep as part of a suggestion only if room. Probably skip to keep findings meaningful.
  - ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO 0.68 — magic constant documented in comment. Fine.
  - `resample(master, size, path)` uses `master.resize` for each size — LANCZOS downscale from 1024 directly to each target — good quality (single-step).
  - iOS 1024 marketing icon: RGB no alpha — App Store compliant. Good.
  - The script has `print` — fine for a CLI tool.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the DM Tools app logo + all launcher icon sizes.

Source artwork: the Android robot logo, provided by the ticket requester
(https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Android_robot.svg/200px-Android_robot.svg.png
— same SVG rendered at 960px, the largest Wikimedia-served size; committed at
tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png). The Android robot is reproduced from
work created and shared by Google, used according to the Creative Commons 3.0
Attribution License.

The robot is centered on an opaque white square badge (platform icon masks
require an opaque square; the badge keeps Android and iOS consistent), and
all sizes are emitted:

  - assets/images/app_logo.png           (1024x1024 master, in-app)
  - android mipmap ic_launcher.png        (48/72/96/144/192)
  - iOS AppIcon.appiconset PNGs           (all sizes in Contents.json)

Deterministic: no randomness, no network (uses the committed source).
"""
from PIL import Image
import os

MASTER = 1024
ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO = 0.68          # robot height as a fraction of the badge
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SOURCE = os.path.join(ROOT, 'tool/logo_source/android_robot_960.png')


def build_master():
    robot = Image.open(SOURCE).convert('RGBA')
    h = round(MASTER * ROBOT_HEIGHT_RATIO)
    w = round(h * robot.width / robot.height)
    robot = robot.resize((w, h), Image.LANCZOS)

    badge = Image.new('RGB', (MASTER, MASTER), (255, 255, 255))
    offset = ((MASTER - w) // 2, (MASTER - h) // 2)
    badge.paste(robot, offset, robot)   # paste with alpha as mask
    return badge


def resample(master, size, path):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    out = master.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS)
    out.save(path, 'PNG')
    print(f'wrote {path} ({size}x{size})')


def main():
    master = build_master()

    resample(master, MASTER, os.path.join(ROOT, 'assets/images/app_logo.png'))

    android = [
        ('mipmap-mdpi', 48), ('mipmap-hdpi', 72), ('mipmap-xhdpi', 96),
        ('mipmap-xxhdpi', 144), ('mipmap-xxxhdpi', 192),
    ]
    for density, size in android:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'android/app/src/main/res/{density}/ic_launcher.png'))

    ios_sizes = [
        ('Icon-App-20x20@1x', 20), ('Icon-App-20x20@2x', 40),
        ('Icon-App-20x20@3x', 60), ('Icon-App-29x29@1x', 29),
        ('Icon-App-29x29@2x', 58), ('Icon-App-29x29@3x', 87),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@1x', 40), ('Icon-App-40x40@2x', 80),
        ('Icon-App-40x40@3x', 120), ('Icon-App-60x60@2x', 120),
        ('Icon-App-60x60@3x', 180), ('Icon-App-76x76@1x', 76),
        ('Icon-App-76x76@2x', 152), ('Icon-App-83.5x83.5@2x', 167),
        ('Icon-App-1024x1024@1x', 1024),
    ]
    for name, size in ios_sizes:
        resample(master, size, os.path.join(
            ROOT, f'ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/{name}.png'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

name: CI

on:

  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

=== README ===
# dm_tools_app_example

Flutter mobile app (Android + iOS) with a login page: email/password sign-in,
**Remember me** session persistence, Google sign-in, and Sign in with Apple.

## Run

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter run            # device or emulator with Android/iOS target
flutter test           # unit + widget tests
flutter analyze
```

## Architecture

- `lib/domain/` — `AuthUser`, `AuthException`, credential validation rules
- `lib/services/` — `AuthGateway` (provider operations) → `DefaultAuthService`
  (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`)
- `lib/ui/` — `LoginPage` (form, remember-me, federated buttons), `HomePage`

Sign-in flows delegate to `AuthGateway`; the service persists the session when
**Remember me** is on, and `DmToolsApp` restores it on startup (login page is
skipped when a session exists).

## Provider setup

- **Google** — `google_sign_in` 7.x needs an OAuth client for Android
  (`google-services.json` / SHA-1 in the console) and iOS (URL scheme from the
  client ID). Without it the button compiles but sign-in fails at runtime.
- **Apple** — the `com.apple.developer.applesignin` entitlement is already
  wired into `ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements` and the Xcode project; enable the
  capability for your App ID in the Apple developer portal. The button is
  hidden automatically where Sign in with Apple is unavailable.
- **Email/password** — local stub (no backend); replace the body of
  `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` with a real identity API call.
- Password managers / autofill: the form uses an `AutofillGroup` and finishes
  the autofill context on success, so platforms that support it offer to save
  and later autofill credentials.
